transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I suppose I’m here because I’m having a harder time keeping things in order than I’d like to admit. It sounds silly, maybe, but my kitchen table is just covered with papers—my husband’s appointment things, church flyers, notes from the senior center, little half-finished lists I’ve made. And I sit down meaning to sort it all out, but then I can’t seem to decide what to do first, and before I know it the whole day’s gone. I’m not sure if that’s the sort of thing you mean, but it’s been really getting to me.
Have you been having trouble with your memory?

A little, yes… though I don’t know if I’d call it memory exactly, maybe just not keeping up with things the way I should. I’ve missed returning calls, and I’ll put a bill down under a stack of mail and then realize later I never took care of it. I’ve also forgotten errands I told my daughter I’d do, which makes me feel awful.

And with my husband’s appointments, more than once I thought I had confirmed something, and then found out too late that I hadn’t. I’m embarrassed to say that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
When you were a child in school, did you often have trouble staying organized?

Yes… I think so, though I suppose at the time people just thought I was a bit dreamy or careless. I did well enough, so it didn’t seem like a serious problem, but I remember teachers writing things like that I was “bright but careless.” I’d forget books or homework, and I needed reminding to finish my seatwork before I could go outside.

That sounds a little silly after all these years, but yes, I guess it was there even when I was little.
Compared with how you were 10 years ago, have these problems with organizing things and keeping track of tasks gotten noticeably worse?

Yes… I think it has been worse, at least noticeably so. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it’s really been causing this much trouble for about a year and three months now, since my husband started needing regular help with his appointments and day-to-day arrangements. Before that I had my little habits and piles, but it didn’t feel quite so unmanageable.
Have you gotten lost in places that used to be familiar to you?
No, I don’t think so. Not really. I mean, I might take a wrong turn now and then, but I haven’t gotten lost in places I know. At least not that I’ve noticed. Is that what you mean?
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

I… I’m not sure I’d call it depressed, exactly. I mean, I have my off days, like anyone, and I can get discouraged. But most days? I don’t think so. At least, I haven’t thought of it that way. Does that make sense?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot more than most people seem to?

I don’t think so… not more than most people, anyway. I do worry about things, of course, but I’ve always thought that was just normal life stuff. I’m not sure I’d say it’s excessive. Does that answer it okay?
Have you started having trouble managing your finances?

A little, maybe… I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. I haven’t, you know, ruined anything, but I have left bills sitting under a stack of mail and then realized later I hadn’t dealt with them. And I’ve missed returning calls about things like that. So yes, I guess there’s been some trouble keeping up with it, if that’s what you mean.
Have you had a stroke?
No, not that I know of. I don’t believe I’ve ever had a stroke.
Have your thinking problems worsened in sudden steps rather than gradually?

I’m not sure I’d describe it as sudden steps, no. It feels more like… well, I notice things here and there, but I can’t point to a clear drop all at once. Unless I’m not understanding what you mean by “sudden steps”?
Do you often forget things that someone told you just a short time earlier?

Yes… I think so, more than I’d like to admit. I mean, not every single time someone tells me something, but I’ll agree to do an errand my daughter asks me about, and then later it’s just gone from my mind. I’ve missed returning calls, and with my husband’s appointments, more than once I realized too late that I never confirmed one. It’s embarrassing… I do try to keep up with things, but I guess I am forgetting things I was just told or asked to do.
Are you needing more help than before with everyday tasks like paying bills, keeping appointments, or managing medications?

A little more, yes… though I hate saying that because I’ve always tried to be the one keeping things organized. I had to step back from leading a big event at the senior center, which was hard. And my daughter has started double-checking bills and appointments for me now—not because I’m completely helpless, I hope, but because she worries I won’t keep it all straight on my own. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Has anyone close to you noticed that your thinking or memory is clearly worse than it used to be?

Yes… my daughter has noticed, I think. She’s kind about it, but she’s started double-checking my bills and appointments because she doesn’t really trust that I’ll keep everything straight on my own anymore.

And I suppose having to give up leading that big event at the senior center was part of it too. I tried to make it sound like I was just stepping back, but… it was getting to be too much to manage. Is that what you mean?
Do you now have trouble remembering recent conversations that would have been easy for you to remember a few years ago?

Yes… I think I do, more than I used to. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I’ll be told something and then later I realize I didn’t hold onto it.

Like I’ve missed returning calls, or I’ll leave bills under a stack of mail and forget they’re there. My daughter will ask me to do an errand and I’ll say yes, of course, and then it just slips away. And with my husband’s appointments, more than once I realized too late that I never confirmed one.

A few years ago I think I would’ve kept those things straight more easily. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Before this past year, were these problems with staying organized and keeping track of tasks present throughout your adult life?

Yes… I suppose they were, though I didn’t really think of it that way at the time. Even when I was a little girl, teachers would write things like I was bright, but careless… that I forgot my books or homework, and needed reminders to finish my seatwork before I could go outside.

I always felt a bit embarrassed by that, so I tried to just say I was “not very organized,” but yes, it does go back a long way. Is that the kind of history you’re asking about?
Has your daughter said that your memory is getting worse than it used to be?

Yes… she has, though she says it gently. She doesn’t really put it as “your memory is getting worse,” but she’s started double-checking my bills and appointments because she doesn’t quite trust that I’ll keep it all straight on my own.

And, well… I did have to step away from leading that big event at the senior center. I told people it was just time, but honestly, keeping track of everything had become too much. I hope that makes sense.
Do you often repeat the same question because you don’t remember that it was already answered?

I don’t think I do that very often… at least, no one has really pointed it out to me. I might ask for clarification if I’m not sure I understood something, but I don’t notice myself asking the exact same question over and over because I forgot the answer.

If anything, I’d probably need my daughter to tell you if she’s noticed it more than I have. Is that all right to say?
Has your daughter told you that these problems are clearly worse than they were a few years ago?

Yes… I think she would say that, though maybe not in a harsh way. It’s really been causing this much trouble for about a year and three months, I’d say—since my husband started needing regular help with his appointments and daily arrangements.

Before that I managed better, or at least I made it look like I did. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you started missing doses or making mistakes with your medications?

I… I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. With medications, I try to be careful. But I have been forgetting other things more than I’d like—returning calls, leaving bills under a stack of mail, little errands I told my daughter I’d do.

And with my husband’s appointments, more than once I’ve realized too late that I never confirmed one. So… I suppose it wouldn’t surprise me if I’ve made some mistakes here and there. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel you are having more trouble learning new information than you used to?

I’m not completely sure. I don’t think I’d say I can’t learn new things, exactly… but maybe I need things repeated or written down more than I used to.

It’s hard for me to tell whether that’s “learning” or just me not paying close enough attention the first time. I don’t want to exaggerate it. Does that make sense?

I’m not completely sure. I don’t think I’d say I can’t learn new things, exactly… but maybe I need things repeated or written down more than I used to.

It’s hard for me to tell whether that’s “learning” or just me not paying close enough attention the first time. I don’t want to exaggerate it. Does that make sense?

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking help today
opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a lifelong history of disorganization and inattentive traits consistent with possible ADHD, but the interview establishes a clear recent worsening over the past 1 year and 3 months with decline from prior baseline, prominent recent-memory difficulties, corroboration by her daughter, and reduced ability to manage instrumental daily tasks such as bills and appointments. This pattern is more consistent with an acquired cognitive disorder than stable ADHD symptoms alone. Stroke, stepwise decline, depression, and excessive anxiety were not supported in the interview.
